questions.text: Quick Revision - Asexual and Sexual Reproduction

definitionBean.title: Asexual and Sexual Reproduction
definitionBean.definition: The process by which living organisms produce new individuals similar to themselves is called 'Reproduction'. Reproduction occurring through a single parent is 'asexual', and through the fusion of male and female gametes is 'sexual'.
definitionBean.explanation: In asexual reproduction, variations during DNA replication are low (e.g., fission, budding, regeneration), whereas in sexual reproduction, involvement of two parents generates higher genetic variations helpful for evolution.
importantPoints: Asexual reproduction: Single organism takes part, offspring is a clone
Sexual reproduction: Fusion of male and female gametes (Fertilization) takes place
Fission (Amoeba) and Budding (Hydra/Yeast) are asexual methods
Sexual reproduction is found in flowering plants and higher animals

questions.text: Quick Revision - Reproduction in Flower and Human Reproductive System

definitionBean.title: Reproduction in Flower and Human Reproductive System
definitionBean.definition: A flower is the reproductive organ of plants containing stamen (male) and carpel (female); and in humans, reproduction is carried out via the male reproductive system (testes) and female reproductive system (ovaries).
definitionBean.explanation: After pollination, pollen grains reach the stigma and form a zygote through fertilization. In humans, fertilization takes place in the fallopian tube.
importantPoints: Stamen: Production of pollen grains (male gamete)
Human Testes: Sperm production and testosterone hormone
Human Ovaries: Ovum production and estrogen hormone

parts.statement: Write differences between asexual and sexual reproduction. Why is reproduction necessary for organisms?
parts.correct_answer: Asexual involves one parent, sexual involves two parents.
parts.explanation: In asexual reproduction, only a single parent takes part and gametes are not formed, whereas in sexual reproduction, two parents (male and female) take part and fusion of gametes occurs. Reproduction is necessary to maintain the existence and continuity of species of organisms.

parts.statement: Explain fission and regeneration with examples.
parts.explanation: In fission, a single organism divides into two or more parts (e.g., Amoeba). In regeneration, if an organism is cut due to any reason, its cut pieces develop into new organisms (e.g., Planaria or Hydra).

parts.statement: Draw a labeled diagram of an ideal flower and describe its main reproductive organs.
parts.correct_answer: Stamen and carpel are main reproductive organs of a flower.
parts.explanation: The main reproductive organs of a flower are the stamen (male organ, containing anther) and carpel (female organ, containing stigma, style, and ovary).

parts.statement: Clarify the difference between self-pollination and cross-pollination.
parts.correct_answer: Self-pollination occurs within same flower/plant, cross-pollination between different plants.
parts.explanation: When pollen grains of a flower reach the stigma of the same flower or another flower of the same plant, self-pollination occurs; when pollen grains of a flower go to the stigma of a flower of another plant, it is called cross-pollination.

parts.statement: Name the main organs of the human male reproductive system and state the functions of the testes.
parts.correct_answer: Testes, vas deferens, penis; testes produce sperm.
parts.explanation: Main organs of the human male reproductive system: Testes, vas deferens, and penis. The primary function of the testes is to produce male gametes (sperm) and secrete the testosterone hormone.

parts.statement: Where does the process of fertilization take place in the human female reproductive system?
parts.explanation: In human females, fertilization (fusion of sperm and ovum) takes place in the fallopian tube (oviduct), after which the zygote gets implanted in the uterus.
